parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/app.module.ts falls under the presentation layer because of the **/*.module.ts pattern. In NestJS, module files are where the app is wired together. This file is the root module: it imports feature modules, registers config loaders, sets up i18n and picks which database module to load. It has no business rules, no domain logic and no request handling. The one part that touches persistence is the `infrastructureDatabaseModule` block, which uses `isDocumentDatabase` to choose between `MongooseModule.forRootAsync` and `TypeOrmModule.forRootAsync`. That block hands the real setup to `MongooseConfigService` or `TypeOrmConfigService`, and its `dataSourceFactory` is the standard one-line `new DataSource(options).initialize()`. This is how the framework registers modules, not repository or query code, so it belongs in a module file. The rubric's Fail examples are business rules in presentation or infrastructure, or persistence or framework logic in domain. Neither applies here, so the file's responsibilities fit the role a module file plays in the presentation layer. Confidence is moderate, because a stricter reading could call the database-selection block infrastructure configuration.
